Input.Content:
# Component inspection comparison
A supplier reviewed three shipments using two independent acceptance dimensions: dimensional tolerance and surface finish. Shipment Larch met tolerance on all 40 inspected components but 6 had surface scratches; it failed finish acceptance. Shipment Birch had no scratches among 40 inspected components but 4 were outside tolerance; it failed dimensional acceptance. Shipment Hazel passed both dimensions on all 40 inspected components. Passing one dimension does not imply passing the other.
Inspectors selected accessible top-layer components rather than a random sample of the shipments. No counts for uninspected lower layers are available. The supplier replaced packing foam after Larch, but Birch also used a different machining batch; no isolated foam-effect test was done.
The report recommends a randomized deeper inspection before changing the acceptance rule. This recommendation has not been tested. It does not recommend dropping either dimension. A separate label-printing delay affected Hazel delivery timing, not either inspected quality dimension.

Idea.Title: Why two acceptance dimensions must remain separate
Idea.Description: Use the contrasting shipments to explain separate dimensions and the limits of the sample and proposed follow-up.
Idea.Rationale: Separate supported observations from stronger conclusions and preserve the relevant contrast.
Idea.Evidence: Larch and Birch failed for the same reason; the foam change solved shipment quality.
